Definition: feminine of G1672; a Grecian (i.e. non-Jewish) woman:--Greek.
BiblicalUsage: Hellenis is a Greek woman, a Gentile woman, and it appears twice, both times for women who believe. In Acts 17:12 honourable women which were Greeks believe at Berea, and in Mark 7:26 the woman who begs Jesus for her daughter is a Greek, a Syrophoenician by nation.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two women belong together in the story: one believes the preaching at Berea, the other will not stop asking until her daughter is healed, and neither of them was supposed to be in the story at all.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
